supporting_observations.claim: At 13:41 UTC, ivy.chen ran PowerShell from Explorer to compress \\FILE-NWD-01\Shared\Clients into C:\Users\ivy.chen\AppData\Local\Temp\c.zip; Sysmon recorded creation of the archive.

At 13:44 UTC, ivy.chen launched Edge to quickshare-drop.net. The proxy subsequently recorded a 51,000,000-byte client-to-server transfer to that domain, and Zeek independently recorded approximately 51 MB outbound through the proxy during the same connection.

The sequence of archiving a shared Clients directory and then sending a large outbound transfer to a file-sharing domain not listed among the organization's approved services strongly supports an attempted data exfiltration finding.
A separate small Edge connection to onedrive.live.com was recorded; OneDrive is listed as approved, and this connection does not account for the 51 MB transfer to quickshare-drop.net.

A user-context process named KB5034441_update.exe ran from C:\Windows\Temp with a quiet-install argument and later exited; the available records do not establish its authenticity or relationship to the transfer.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records a CONNECT tunnel and byte counts, while the associated Zeek connection records traffic to the proxy; the available records do not expose the encrypted transfer payload or identify the exact uploaded file.

The listed winsec and Sysmon collection outage applies to WS-NBLAKE-01 from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, not WS-ICHEN-01. The outage limits visibility on that other host but does not explain the observed transfer from WS-ICHEN-01.
claims_not_established: That c.zip, or any particular file from the Clients directory, was the content of the outbound transfer.
What data was transferred, whether it contained sensitive information, or whether the transfer completed as an upload of a specific file.
Who was physically operating the workstation; the records associate the activity with ivy.chen's account but do not establish the human actor.
Whether KB5034441_update.exe is malicious or related to the archive or outbound transfer.
The ownership, reputation, or operator of quickshare-drop.net beyond its use for the observed connection.
additional_evidence_needed: Preserve and examine WS-ICHEN-01, including c.zip, source files, browser history and download records, and the hash, signature, and origin of KB5034441_update.exe.
Obtain proxy and TLS inspection records, if available, to determine the upload request details, destination, and transferred content or filename.
Review file-server access and audit records for ivy.chen's access to \\FILE-NWD-01\Shared\Clients and correlate access with archive creation.
Investigate quickshare-drop.net using organizational threat-intelligence and domain ownership or reputation data.
